name: Joseph John Murphy
bio: Joseph John Murphy (1827–1894; dates as printed in the anthology) is represented here by poems from the sacred-verse volume.

The poems here are taken from Alfred H. Miles (ed.), The Poets and the Poetry of the Century (London: Hutchinson, 1891–1897), vol. 10, from the Internet Archive scans of that edition. Spelling is that of the anthology; Miles's biographical essay and extracts from longer poems are omitted, and only poems that could be read cleanly from the scan are included.

poems.title: Eternity
poems.author: Joseph John Murphy
poems.text:
Eternity is not, as men believe,
Before and after us, an endless line.
No; "tis a circle, infinitely great,
All the circumference with creatures thronged
God at the centre dwells, beholding all.
And, as we move in this eternal round
The finite portion which alone we see,
Behind us, is the Past; what lies before
We call the Future. But to Him who dwells
Far in the centre, equally remote
From every point of the circumference,
Both are alike the Future and the Past.
